Tesla Full Self-Driving v14.3.4 in a 2026 Model Y rental — no radar, no ultrasonic sensors, no lidar, just eight cameras, an end-to-end neural network trained by imitation learning, and a distilled student model small enough to run behind the dash. After eight years and $8,000 of Enhanced Autopilot and FSD Capability promises, plus a slow exit to Rivian R1T, R1S and R2, FSD v14 is finally smoother and more confident than the average Uber driver — and, surprisingly, more comfortable than a week of Waymo robotaxi rides around San Francisco. It still botches parking lots, misses freeway exits, invents its own routing instead of using Google Maps or Waze, and parked me nowher
title: Tesla Owes Me $8,000 and Eight Years
